Subject: Post-call: token consumption bucket validation + PO clearance path

Hi Oliver / Procurement,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align on the three usage profiles you mentioned (triage chatbot, patient intake summarization, and analytics enrichment). Quick recap and asks to help us produce a clean SOW/pricing draft: 

1) Monthly consumption band: you described a likely steady-state of ~6–10M tokens/month with bursty spikes (~15M) during pilots. Can you confirm the steady-state band we should model for a 6‑month pilot?

2) Unit economics target: you mentioned a goal of keeping first-year spend below a rough $/1M token threshold for budgeting. If Skyline has a target $/1M tokens, tell us the number we should hit in the quote (we'll show options with and without KV caching and aggressive batching).

3) Procurement thresholds: important for rollout — what PO level requires board approval vs. standard procurement sign-off? You mentioned a $25k internal threshold on the call; please confirm. Also share the procurement contact if different from this thread.

Next steps from our side: we will attach a compact pricing proposal (baseline + two tiered discounts) and a short runbook describing staging canary sizing. If we get the confirmed steady-state band and PO threshold today, Karthik and I can put together a recommend purchase path (month-to-month pilot vs. committed monthly band) for Marissa to review.

Attachments: 20271012-Redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf (baseline, caching, quantization scenarios).

Thanks — Naomi

On Tue, Oct 12, 2027 at 2:03 PM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align on the three usage profiles you mentioned...

Thanks Naomi — short answers below. Appreciate the clear recap.

- Steady-state band: confirm 6–10M tokens/month for budgeting. For the initial 6-week canary we expect ~3–4M tokens/month, then ramp to the band if KPIs hold.
- $/1M target: leadership is comfortable with up to $1,200 per 1M tokens for pilot pricing, provided we have predictable latency and token caps. If you can show a $950 option with caching and a chart of expected latency tradeoffs, that'll be helpful.
- Procurement thresholds: correct — routine POs up to $25k are handled by the procurement team. Anything above $25k goes to the finance committee and can add 2–3 weeks to approval. Our procurement contact is Heather Lin (heather.lin@skylinehealth.com).

Also attaching our procurement checklist (see attachment). We can provision a procurement POC to walk through security and SOC evidence next week.

Oliver
Director, Platform Integrations
Skyline Health

Perfect — thanks for the confirmations, Oliver. Quick reply with proposed next steps so procurement timelines are visible: 

A) Pricing proposal deliverable (attached): three lanes
   - Pilot (month-to-month): modeled on 3–4M tokens/month for first 6 weeks, unit price $1,200/1M tokens. No long-term commitment; ideal for fast proof-of-value.
   - Committed band (6 months): 6–10M tokens/month, blended $950/1M tokens with prefix/KV caching assumptions included.
   - Enterprise commit (12 months): custom blended rate below $800/1M tokens with dedicated capacity options — requires legal/finance review.

B) Procurement path: since POs > $25k require finance committee review, we recommend structuring the initial engagement as a 6-week pilot (pilot cost ~ $3.6k–$4.8k) to avoid the $25k threshold while giving you data to justify a committed band. Karthik will sketch the exact PO line items and payment schedule.

C) Marissa will sign off on discounts for pilots and confirm whether we can extend a one-time 10% onboarding credit for Skyline. Marissa — can you confirm by EOD today?

D) Security & evidence: we'll loop in our security team and share SOC/Security artifacts in a gated Drive link; procurement POC call proposed next Tue.

Action items:
- Karthik: produce line-item PO-friendly pricing and a 6-week pilot invoice draft (by EOD today).
- Marissa: confirm pilot discount/onboarding credit (by EOD).
- Oliver/Heather: confirm they can sign the pilot PO without escalation.

I'll follow up after Karthik drops the PO draft. Thanks all.

— Naomi
